ops.title: Binding hosts must generate $defs-shaped (2020-12) schemas — anthropic strict transform recurses only $defs
ops.body:
Found 2026-07-18 during the Go/Rust bindings build. spawnllm-core's strict-schema transforms are oracle-faithful to Pydantic 2020-12 output: `transform_anthropic` recurses ONLY `$defs` (rust/spawnllm-core/src/schema.rs:51), while the openai `ensure_strict` walks both `$defs` and `definitions` (schema.rs:181,187).

Consequence for any language host implementing extract: if its schema generator emits draft-07 `definitions` (schemars 0.8 hard-codes this shape; even its draft2019_09 setting keeps `#/definitions/`), the CLAUDE dialect silently ships every referenced definition UN-strictified — the `definitions` subtree gets stringified into a description as "leftover keywords" and the `#/definitions/...` refs dangle. The call still "works", so end-to-end tests don't catch it.

Rules for hosts (current and future bindings):
1. Generate 2020-12 / `$defs`-shaped schemas: Rust uses schemars ≥1 (1.2.x); Go uses invopop/jsonschema (emits $defs natively).
2. Every host carries a receives-side assertion test: extract a nested/referenced struct through fake CLIs and assert `additionalProperties:false` in the root AND inside every `$defs` entry of the schema the fake claude (`--json-schema` argv) and fake codex (`--output-schema` file) actually receive. Conformance vectors cannot cover this — host schema generation sits outside the oracle by design.
